scalars.scalar_value: Two years of full-time equivalent experience in: Counseling students with disabilities; or Counseling in industry, government, public agencies, military, or private social welfare organizations serving individuals with disabilities.

items.item_text: 01. How would you describe your level of education? Options: High School/GED | Some College | Associates Degree | Bachelors Degree | Masters Degree | Doctorate | None of the Above
02. How many years full time equivalent work experience do you have in the field for which you are applying? Options: 0-1 years | 1-2 years | 3-5 years | 5-10 years | More than 10 years
03. Have you attached your CV including education, experience, professional organizations, and accomplishments? Options: Yes | No
04. Have you attached your letter of interest that succinctly addresses how your experience and professional qualifications prepare you for this position? Options: Yes | No

05. Have you provided three (3) professional or academic references who can speak to your qualifications for the position and their contact information? (personal references will not be accepted). Options: Yes | No
06. Have you attached photo copies of all transcripts? (a foreign transcript evaluation must be attached if applicable. Official copies of transcripts are required upon employment) Options: Yes | No
07. Are you applying through equivalency? Options: Yes | No

08. If you are applying through equivalency, have you submitted the Mendocino College equivalency form, found at: https://www.mendocino.edu/about/administration/administrative-departments/human-resources#tabs-29904 Options: Yes | No | Not Applicable - I am not applying through equivalency

09. IMPORTANT: All applicants are required to submit requested application materials as defined in the application procedure. Supplemental question(s)/writing prompts will provide information about your background and experience related to this position and will be used in the screening and selection process. Be concise, yet specific. "See resume" or links will not be accepted as a substitute for your responses to these prompts. Submit your response(s) in the attachments section of the application. For more details, please refer to the Application Procedures section of the job announcement. If you fail to submit the additional information, your application will be considered incomplete and will not be moved forward for the screening process. Question: I have read and understand the required documentation upload process. Options: Yes | No

Two years of full-time equivalent experience in: Counseling students with disabilities; or Counseling in industry, government, public agencies, military, or private social welfare organizations serving individuals with disabilities.
Develops, implements, and oversees department services; coordinates with assigned staff on DSPS program projects, resources, and activities;
Lead in planning, implementing, and evaluating the DSPS program through Program Review;
Lead the DSPS department in developing and assessing Service Learning Outcomes;

Oversees specialized services and contracts, such as Deaf and Hard of Hearing services; Plan, organize, develop program activities, complete program reports, and maintain and monitor the program budget;
Serves as the College DSPS liaison for the respective geographic feeder schools and agencies;
Monitors District compliance with state and federal laws and policies related to the DSPS and Title 5 CCR;
Coordinates and supports DSPS staff in delivering appropriate services to college students who have verified disabilities;
Coordinates with other college staff who work to support accessibility such as Distance Education Coordinator and Web & Instructional Designer;
Provides information about professional resources and training for faculty in creating accessible materials in their classroom and online courses;
Facilitates access to training and other support measures with staff and faculty to specialized software and applicable technology;
Manages student files and documentation as mandated by the Chancellor’s Office;
Collaborates with appropriate stakeholders regarding special class instruction;
Facilitates public information and college communications concerning the DSPS;
Attends meetings, including local, state, and regional workshops and seminars, to stay current on relevant issues; serves on college committees;
Performs other duties as assigned.
Fifteen (15) semester units of upper-division or graduate coursework related to people with disabilities; or
DSPS/DRC programs, accommodations, and student support services.
Completion of six (6) semester units, or the equivalent, of graduate-level counseling practicum or fieldwork in a postsecondary DSPS program or a program serving individuals with disabilities; or
Program planning, assessment, Service Area Review, and continuous improvement processes.
Counseling students with disabilities; or
Budget development, fiscal management, and reporting practices.
Counseling in industry, government, public agencies, military, or private social welfare organizations serving individuals with disabilities.
Assistive technology, accessibility standards, and inclusive educational practices.
Community resources, contracted services, and shared governance processes.
Plan, implement, coordinate, and evaluate DSPS/DRC programs, services, and initiatives.
Lead assessment, Service Area Review, outcomes evaluation, and program improvement efforts.
Manage budgets, reports, contracts, records, and compliance activities.
Coordinate accommodations, assistive technology, and support services for students with disabilities.
Collaborate with faculty, staff, community agencies, and educational partners.
Provide training, outreach, consultation, and leadership related to accessibility and inclusion.
Serve effectively on committees and support institutional planning and governance activities.
Federal and state disability laws, DSPS regulations, Title 5, and Chancellor's Office requirements.
